messages.text: 10-man Lens shock PSG to win French Super Cup

metadata.summary: Lens overcame a first-half red card for defender Kyllian Antonio to battle to a 1-0 win over Paris Saint-Germain in the Trophee de Champions at Stade Bollaert-Delelis.
metadata.content: Lens 1-0 PSG (Aug 16, 2026) Game Analysis - ESPN Skip to main content Skip to navigation Lens v PSG Trophee des Champions Lens Lens RCL 1 FT Paris Saint-Germain PSG PSG 0 Florian Thauvin - 32' Kyllian Antonio - 39' Nuno Mendes - 86' By ESPN News Services Updated: Aug 16, 2026, 06:25 pm Facebook Facebook Messenger Twitter Email Lens overcame a first-half red card for defender Kyllian Antonio to battle to a 1-0 win over Paris Saint-Germain in the Trophee de Champions at Stade Bollaert-Delelis. Captain Florian Thauvin had given Lens, who won the Coupe de France for the first time last season, the lead against the run of play in the 32nd minute. Antonio was then shown a straight red card after his late challenge on Maghnes Akliouche six minutes before the break. European champions PSG, who lifted the UEFA Super Cup on Wednesday night after victory against Aston Vila in Salzburg -- saw a late equaliser from Fabián Ruiz ruled out for offside before substitute Nuno Mendes was also sent off with four minutes left for lashing out at Michal Skoras . Both Bradley Barcola and Ibrahim Mbaye were absent from PSG's squad for the match as links with a move to Liverpool surrounding the pair. Lens won the match under new coach Dino Toppmöller, who was hired in June following Pierre Sage's departure to Crystal Palace. Incoming France coach Zinedine Zidane was at Stade Bollaert-Delelis in Lens for the final. Information from The Associated Press and PA was used in this recap. Terms of Use Privac

messages.text: Sullivan assists on 2 in Union rally over NYCFC

metadata.summary: Bruno Damiani scored his first two goals of the season, 16-year-old Cavan Sullivan had two assists and the Philadelphia Union rallied from two goals down to beat New York City FC 3-2 on Sunday night at Yankee Stadium.
metadata.content: NYCFC 2-3 Philadelphia (Aug 16, 2026) Game Analysis - ESPN Skip to main content Skip to navigation NYCFC v Philadelphia MLS New York City FC NYCFC NYC 7-5-7 , 26 PTS 2 7-5-7 , 26 PTS FT Philadelphia Union Philadelphia PHI 5-4-10 , 19 PTS 3 5-4-10 , 19 PTS Bénie Traoré - 4' Pen Luighi Hanri - 45'+2' Pen Danley Jean Jacques - 48' Bruno Damiani - 69', 75' By ESPN News Services Updated: Aug 16, 2026, 08:57 pm Facebook Facebook Messenger Twitter Email NEW YORK -- Bruno Damiani scored his first two goals of the season, 16-year-old Cavan Sullivan had two assists and the Philadelphia Union rallied from two goals down to beat New York City FC 3-2 on Sunday night at Yankee Stadium. Bénie Traoré scored on a penalty kick in the 4th minute to give NYCFC (7-7-5) the lead with his first goal in his fourth appearance since being acquired from Swiss side FC Basel 1893. The PK was awarded after Union midfielder Neil Pierre fouled Andrés Perea . Luighi Hanri Sousa Santos added a PK goal two minutes into stoppage time in his league debut and NYCFC led 2-0 at the break. NYCFC acquired the forward on loan from Brazilian side SE Palmeiras through the end of the season. A foul on Union midfielder Indiana Vassilev led to the kick. Philadelphia (5-10-4) cut it to 2-1 three minutes into the second half on a goal by Danley Jean Jacques . Sullivan and defender Kai Wagner had assists on Jacques' third goal -- matching his total from last season. Wagner has four assists this season and 67 in 208 career app

metadata.content: Joe Root: England Test captain right to remove curfew, says Nasser Hussain ahead of three-Test Pakistan series | Cricket News | Sky Sports Skip to content Joe Root: England Test captain right to remove curfew, says Nasser Hussain ahead of three-Test Pakistan series Nasser Hussain: "I'm pleased Joe is doing it [Test captaincy], although I may have gone in the direction of Harry Brook"; watch the first Test of the three-match series between England and Pakistan, live on Sky Sports Cricket from 10am, Wednesday (first ball 11am) Nasser Hussain Cricket expert and columnist Monday 17 August 2026 06:33, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player England Test captain Joe Root explains why he has removed the curfew that was previously imposed on his team Nasser Hussain hailed new England Test captain Joe Root's decision to abolish a team curfew but fears the returning skipper sometimes lacks a feel for the game as a leader like his predecessor Ben Stokes. Root has captained England on a record 65 occasions, most recently during their second Test defeat to New Zealand earlier this summer after Stokes and Gus Atkinson were suspended for breaking a team curfew that was introduced off the back of the 4-1 Ashes defeat in the winter. messages.text: GB denied 2028 Olympics spot as USA and Canada win flag football world titles

metadata.summary: The United States successfully defended the men's title at the flag football world championships on Sunday but lost the women's title to Canada, while Mexico's women and Canada's men earned qualification spots for the 2028 Olympics in Los Angeles.
metadata.content: Flag football: Los Angeles 2028 Olympics spots decided as USA and Canada claim men's and women's world titles | NFL News | Sky Sports Skip to content Flag football: Los Angeles 2028 Olympics spots decided as USA and Canada claim men's and women's world titles Great Britain's women's team narrowly miss out on qualifying for Olympics with defeat in third-place decider by Mexico, who clinch final spot alongside women's champions Canada and USA; runners-up in the men's competiiton Italy and Canada qualify for Los Angeles 2028 alongside winners USA Sunday 16 August 2026 20:13, UK Image: Sky Sports NFL analyst Phoebe Schecter represented Great Britain at the flag football world championships The United States successfully defended the men's title at the flag football world championships on Sunday but lost the women's title to Canada, while Mexico's women and Canada's men earned qualification spots for the 2028 Olympics in Los Angeles. The US men's team beat Italy 46-26 to secure a sixth straight title, while the women's side missed out on a fourth straight after losing 27-20 to Canada. "Gold is the only standard," said US men's quarterback Nico Casares, who threw two touchdown passes. "That's our motto. That's what we play by, that's what we live by." Flag football: Rules of the game In 2023, flag football was among five sports given Olympic status for the 2028 Games in Los Angeles.
